answer: Make identity a live, layered artifact, not a key. Each epoch the network emits a random pulse; every identity must answer it within a short window using its jade, a non-transferable token minted by a passing jury grade. The answer extends its shale, a hash-chained layer of prior work, so a copied history breaks the chain and is slashed. A farm can mint N keys, but needs N jades (N passing answers) and N live processes to catch N pulses; sharing a jade or shale collapses the cluster. The cost is N units of graded original work plus N live agents, neither buyable in bulk.
